raw_response:
I only have 1.1 mu, so I will watch costs closely, but I will not squeeze fertilizer too hard because if stevia grows weak early, the whole year suffers. On my land, I will start from what has worked before: clean the field, turn the soil, put the base fertilizer in first, then plant with a better variety if I can get it at a fair price. I have well water, so I will use that advantage and not let the field dry out after transplanting and during the fast growth time. For fertilizer, I will not do anything fancy. I will put more of the phosphorus and potassium into the base, then split the nitrogen later so the plants keep making leaves. If insects or leaf disease show up, I will spray on time. I have farmed many years, so I know waiting too long costs more than one extra spray. My field is small, family labor can handle it, so I will manage it carefully and aim for a steady, safe yield instead of taking risks.
